interface.title: SITA — 13C natural-abundance correction
interface.field: Metabolomics / 13C metabolic flux analysis (GC-MS stable-isotope tracing)
interface.stage_of_work: Data processing: correcting measured GC-MS mass isotopomer distributions for natural isotope abundance before flux analysis
interface.what_it_is_for: Builds the natural-abundance correction matrix for a derivatized GC-MS fragment from its molecular formula and its number of labellable backbone carbons, and optionally applies it to a measured mass distribution vector to give the corrected, normalised MDV*. The web interface corrects for natural abundance only; the unlabelled-biomass correction (mdv_AA) is available only from the Python library.

data.note: Nothing is preloaded and nothing can be uploaded. The worked example (alanine M-57, C11H26NO2Si2, backbone_c=3, MDV 0.6228, 0.1517, 0.0749, 0.1507) is only placeholder text in the fields, so I typed it in by hand. I also made up a second case: formula C14H32NO2Si2 with backbone_c=5 and an invented 6-value MDV. I first labelled it valine M-57, but that is wrong: valine M-57 is C13H30NO2Si2 (backbone_c=5), and C14H32NO2Si2 is the leucine/isoleucine M-57 formula (backbone_c=6). The second case is therefore an arbitrary formula/backbone_c pairing that matches no real fragment. It still shows the tool handling a larger input.

tree.general: Correct measured isotope-label distributions for naturally occurring heavy isotopes so they can be used in downstream flux analysis
tree.specific: Get the 13C natural-abundance correction matrix for a GC-MS fragment and the corrected MDV* from a measured MDV (Nanchen 2007 / Fischer 2004)

children.general: Build the correction operator for one measured item
children.specific: [01] correction matrix: molecular formula + backbone carbons → (backbone_c+1)×(backbone_c+1) matrix. The matrix shown is the one applied to measured data, i.e. the inverse of the correction matrix printed in Nanchen 2007. For alanine M-57 its diagonal is 1.2963, which is 1/0.7715, the paper's diagonal (reviewer's comparison with the values in the repo's tests).

features.name: Formula-driven correction-matrix calculator with matrix table view
features.general: Enter a chemical formula and the number of labellable positions, compute, and read a lower-triangular square matrix whose size follows that parameter. The matrix is the operator applied to measured data, i.e. the inverse of the correction matrix as usually published. The diagonal is underlined, zeros show as dots, and the row under the pointer is highlighted.
features.specific: In [01], type a molecular formula and backbone_c, press compute matrix or Enter, and read the (backbone_c+1)² natural-abundance correction matrix (inverse of Nanchen 2007's matrix; diagonal 1.2963 vs 0.7715 for alanine M-57), with a size label and a 'ready · N ms' status
steps: read the N×N table; hover rows to follow a row across
change backbone_c and recompute to compare sizes and values
serves_tasks: Compute the correction operator for a reference worked example and inspect it
See how the number of labellable positions changes the operator's size and values
Compute the correction operator for a second, different item

features.name: Measured-vector correction with normalised output
features.general: Paste a comma-separated vector of measured fractions or raw counts next to the item's description. The tool checks its length against the expected size, applies the natural-abundance correction, and returns a column vector that sums to 1. No further correction (e.g. for unlabelled biomass) is applied.
features.specific: In [02], type formula, backbone_c and the measured MDV, then press compute mdv* to get MDV* as a (backbone_c+1)×1 table normalised to 1. mdv_AA (unlabelled-biomass correction) is only in the Python library.
steps: paste the measured MDV, comma-separated (fractions or raw intensities)
read the corrected vector, or fix the input from the inline error
serves_tasks: Correct the reference example's measured distribution

not_done: Checking the alanine M-57 result against published values was not done in the run: the interface shows no reference values, and the linked DOIs did not load. The reviewer later compared the run's numbers with the paper's values in the repo's tests (packages/sita-core/tests/test_core.py:24-32). MDV* 0.7730, 0.0371, 0.0183, 0.1715 matches the published 0.7730, 0.0372, 0.0183, 0.1715 within rounding. The matrix diagonal 1.29626 equals 1/0.7715, the inverse of the paper's correction-matrix diagonal. Tool values recorded: diagonal 1.29626, off-diagonals -0.253462, -0.0635074, 0.019948.
No link between the [01] and [02] sections: [02] takes its own formula and backbone_c and does not reuse the matrix from [01]. There is nothing to pass a result between them, so I did not test any.
Space- or semicolon-separated MDVs: the parser accepts commas only (space-separated input gave an error, screens/024.webp). Semicolons were not tried.

The second fragment is not a real fragment. C14H32NO2Si2 was mislabelled as valine M-57: it is the leucine/isoleucine M-57 formula (backbone_c=6), and valine M-57 is C13H30NO2Si2 (backbone_c=5). The run paired C14H32NO2Si2 with backbone_c=5, so its numbers (t4, t7) are not usable for either amino acid.

Stepping backbone carbons with the arrow keys: pressing ArrowUp changed the field from 0 to 1 but did not recompute the matrix, which still showed the 1×1 result for 0 (screens/013.webp). Pressing Enter after stepping was not tried, and the replay did not confirm arrow-key stepping.
